subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the narrow provider-normalized schema-parameter cache from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78664, or fold this issue into the broader prepared-runtime migration before fixing it?
rationale: The remaining choice affects hot-path provider/plugin behavior and cache lifecycle, and the direct PR is conflicting, so automation should not start another implementation path without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt the narrow cache
options.body: Rebase or replace the existing cache PR, keep custom provider hooks bypassed, and require cache-hit plus live or heap-pressure proof before merge.

options.title: Fold into prepared runtime
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader prepared runtime migration and close the direct cache PR only after an equivalent path is ready.

options.title: Wait for live repro
options.body: Keep the issue parked until a current Google/Gemini live repro proves the ban or latency symptom still happens on main.

recommendation.title: Adopt the narrow cache
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace the existing cache PR, keep custom provider hooks bypassed, and require cache-hit plus live or heap-pressure proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest recent history across the plugin SDK provider-tools file and agent runtime/provider execution refactors.
